scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

But recently, there was a bathroom flood, so they had to remodel my section of the house, which means we're running into each other a lot more than before. I used to lock myself in my room most of the time to avoid them, but now that's not possible. One day, my parents went to Costco. When they got home, I was sitting on the couch playing Apex Legends. My mom asked me to get up and help them bring in the groceries. I told her I'd do it in a minute. I was really into the game and didn't notice that they made several trips back and forth. Finally, my dad told me to get my ass up, and I told him I'd do it in a minute. He said, "A minute is now," grabbed the controller out of my hand, and that turned into a huge shouting match. Now, they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday, which is basically impossible. They also brought up my younger brother, who is married with two kids and just got promoted at his job. They have their "golden child," and now they're throwing his success in my face. I mean, I guess I could have gotten up and helped them, but to me, because I pay rent, that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. They ended up making several trips, and my dad got frustrated, leading to a shouting match. Now, they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to find a place by Friday, which is impossible. They're also comparing me to my younger brother, who is successful. So, is it wrong for me to expect that paying rent gives me the right to say no to helping with chores? Or is it reasonable for my parents to expect help since I'm living under their roof? Also, is it fair for them to compare me to my brother? I think part of the issue is the expectation of help. But I also have the right to relax and enjoy my free time, especially after a long day. The shouting match escalated things, and now they're threatening to leave me without a place to live. That seems extreme. But maybe they felt disrespected when I didn't help immediately. I also feel hurt that they're comparing me to my brother, who is doing well. I think I might be partially at fault for not helping when they asked, but I also feel like they overreacted by threatening to leave me without a place to live. It's a tough situation. Overall, I think both sides have some responsibility here.
